issues.failure_explanation: A proper lower-semicontinuous (closed) convex function need not have a closed domain: e.g., $p(x) = -\log x$ for $x>0$ and $p(x)=+\infty$ for $x\le 0$ is closed, proper and convex, yet $\dom p=(0,\infty)$ is not closed. Hence the closedness of $\cX=\dom p$ used in the proof of Lemma lem:open is an omitted hypothesis that the proof assumes without establishing it.

failure_location.quote: It then follows from $x^k \to x$ and the closedness of $\cX$ that $x\in\cX$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that $\cX$ is closed (equivalently, that $\dom p$ is closed) to Assumption (ii); alternatively replace $\cX$ by its closure in the definitions of $\cX_\epsilon$ and $\cX^\rc_\epsilon$. No other changes are needed.
issues.overall_effect: One step of the proof of Lemma lem:open (openness of $\cU_\epsilon$) is unjustified as written; the lemma's conclusion, and transitively the proof of Theorem thm:Phi_smooth which cites it, remain valid once the hypothesis is added.
issues.title: Proof of Lemma lem:open invokes closedness of $\cX$, which Assumption (ii) does not guarantee
issues.why_classification: A one-clause hypothesis addition (a standard local condition) restores the proof; problems with non-closed $\dom p$ are a degenerate boundary case, so the method, conclusions, rates, and advertised scope all survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: It is also well-known that $\partial (\phi_1 + \phi_2)(x) = \nabla \phi_1(x) + \partial \phi_2(x)$ if $\phi_1$ is differentiable and $\phi_2$ is locally Lipschitz continuous at $x$
Additionally, notice that $\partial F^*$ and $\partial p$ are outer semicontinuous on $\cX$.  Hence, $\partial \Psi$ is outer semicontinuous on $\cX$

issues.failure_explanation: The equality $\partial(F^*+p)(x)=\partial F^*(x)+\partial p(x)$ for Clarke subdifferentials requires the first function to be differentiable at $x$ (as the paper's own notation section correctly states) or an additional qualification; it is false for merely Lipschitz first functions: for $F^*(x)=-|x|$ and $p(x)=|x|$ at $x=0$, $\partial(F^*+p)(0)=\{0\}$ while $\partial F^*(0)+\partial p(0)=[-1,1]+[-1,1]=[-2,2]$. Since Lemma lem:Lips gives only Lipschitz continuity of $F^*$, the asserted equality — and with it the outer semicontinuity of $\partial\Psi$ and the openness of $\cU_\epsilon$ — is unjustified as written. The conclusion is nonetheless true: $\partial\Psi$ is outer semicontinuous on $\cX$ by a direct argument (Clarke's o.s.c. theorem applies on $\operatorname{int}\cX$ where $\Psi$ is locally Lipschitz; at boundary points of $\dom p$, if $\partial p(x_0)\neq\emptyset$ then $\partial p$ is locally bounded there so $\partial\Psi(x_0)$ is closed and a Carathéodory/diagonalization argument from the limit-of-gradients definition yields $s\in\partial\Psi(x_0)$, while $\partial p(x_0)=\emptyset$ forces nearby subgradients to escape to infinity).

failure_location.quote: By this and $\Psi=F^*+p$, one has $\partial \Psi=\partial F^*+\partial p$ on $\cX$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the sum-rule step with a direct proof that $\partial\Psi$ is outer semicontinuous on $\cX$ from the limit-of-gradients definition (case analysis on $\operatorname{int}\cX$ versus the boundary of $\dom p$, as described in the failure explanation); no other part of the paper needs changes.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma lem:open contains a false inference, so the openness of $\cU_\epsilon$ is unproved as written; the lemma's conclusion and the conclusions of Theorem thm:Phi_smooth and the downstream complexity theorems remain valid once the step is replaced by a direct outer-semicontinuity argument.
issues.title: Proof of Lemma lem:open asserts a false Clarke sum rule for a merely Lipschitz $F^*$
issues.why_classification: The load-bearing equality is false in general, so the proof needs a contained replacement argument (a new outer-semicontinuity proof for a Lipschitz-plus-convex sum); however no result is abandoned, no regime is excluded, and all main conclusions and rates are unchanged, so the resolution avoids new global proof architecture and major loss.
